doc: A browser.private card for a LAN literal names the target, the pinned address and its class in its title, says that any page could then send requests to it, and offers the target's /24 on its port and all private as well as the one target (for the session; the plan's widths only with a plan). What makes it fail: a private card that offers only one target for a literal, or widths without saying what they open.

data.title: s1 wants to open 192.168.1.20:8080 → 192.168.1.20:8080 (your LAN)
data.body: Any page the agent opens could then send requests to it, including ones that change things

choices.label: Allow 192.168.1.0/24 on port 8080 for this session

sql: select (select group_concat(json_extract(value, '$.id'), ' ') from json_each(card.data, '$.choices')), json_extract(data, '$.body') is not null from card where id = $c1
select (select group_concat(json_extract(value, '$.id'), ' ') from json_each(card.data, '$.choices')) from card where id = $c2
rows: once session plan session/cidr plan/cidr session/all-private plan/all-private refuse
